chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ali ibn Uqbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), concerning

a man upon whom death arrived, so he freed a slave belonging to him, and there was no other [slave] for him. The heirs refused to approve that. How is the judgment regarding him? He (peace be upon him) said: Only one-third of him is freed, and the rest belongs to the heirs, and the heirs have more right to that, and to them belongs what remains.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a single slave when a person is on their deathbed?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the application of the one-third estate rule (khums al-mirath) specifically to manumission, establishing that the freed slave's value is deducted from the deceased's share before distribution to heirs. It highlights the Shia juristic view that heirs retain ownership of the remaining two-thirds, allowing them to keep the slave or liquidate the asset, thereby balancing the dying person's charitable intent with the heirs' financial rights.
